issues.description: Class name mismatch between the UML in the problem statement and the provided code: the UML block in problem_statement.md declares the class as 'Course' (line 63) while both the template and the solution define the class as 'Lecture' (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java, line 3). This naming divergence can confuse students about which class they should implement and where the attributes listed in the UML belong.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the class name consistent across all artifacts. Update the UML block in problem_statement.md to declare 'class Lecture { ... }' instead of 'class Course', and keep the attribute names as-is. Alternatively, if 'Course' was intended, rename the template and solution classes/files to 'Course' and update the textual references. Prefer keeping 'Lecture' (code + text) and changing the UML, as that requires the smallest change to provided code and tests.
